name: Mississippi Pot Roast Bowls
writer_notes: SELECTOR: The single most-searched chuck roast recipe in America and not in the catalog. Shreds clean, weighs and divides at 14 servings over mashed potatoes. Source pages report 418-503 cal for meat+gravy alone across variants; over potatoes it lands ~620 with 40g+ protein. Confidence: high on protein, medium on final assembled calorie count (estimated from meat-only nutrition plus a standard potato base). | HARVEST: Nutrition covers the beef/gravy only; no starch or side in the source ingredient list.
intro_html: Mississippi pot roast is the most searched chuck roast recipe in America, and there is a reason: you put five things in a slow cooker, add no liquid at all, walk away, and come back to beef that falls apart under a fork. Ranch, gravy mix, butter, and pepperoncini do all of it. Each bowl carries {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost).
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Ranch Seasoning Mix, 5.75 tbsp: ~$0.75. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 1oz packets.
Brown Gravy Mix, 1.25 oz: ~$0.57. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 0.87oz packets.
Rice, 4 cups dry: ~$0.86. Buy 1 (covers this batch with some left over).
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.17. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $41.32 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.95 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $45.92 across 14 servings, roughly $3.28 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $5.63 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $51.55. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a dinner with a ten minute prep. The chuck roast is nearly the whole cost, so this is a recipe that rewards buying beef on the dip.
shop_smart: Chuck roast is the correct cut and the cheap one. Do not substitute a lean roast, because there is no added liquid here and the fat in the chuck is what keeps it moist.
Ranch seasoning and gravy mix both come in multi packet boxes that cost less per packet than the singles. They keep in the pantry indefinitely.
A jar of pepperoncini lasts several batches and the brine is half the flavor, so do not drain it entirely.
Butter goes on sale hard around the holidays and freezes for a year. Buy several boxes then and stop paying peak price the rest of the year.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry and season it with salt and black pepper. Set it in the slow cooker whole.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning mix and the brown gravy mix evenly over the top of the roast. Do not stir and do not add water.
Lay the butter on top of the roast in slices so it melts down through the seasonings as it cooks.
Scatter the pepperoncini around and over the roast, along with a few spoonfuls of their brine.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours. Resist opening the lid, since the roast is making its own liquid the whole time.
Shred the beef with two forks directly in the cooker and stir it through the gravy that has collected at the bottom.
Cook the rice separately and keep it plain, because the gravy is doing plenty.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon that weight of shredded beef and gravy into each container, then add the same weight of rice to every one. Each bowl lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Season the chuck roast and set it whole in the slow cooker.
Sprinkle over the ranch and brown gravy mixes with no added liquid.
Top with sliced butter and scatter pepperoncini and a little brine around it.
Cook on low 8 hours without lifting the lid.
Shred the beef into its gravy, cook the rice, and portion into 14 containers.
